title: Loaded Firehouse Sweet Potatoes
seoTitle: Loaded Firehouse Sweet Potatoes | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Baked sweet potatoes topped with seasoned beef, Greek yogurt, and cheese, topping-bar style
subtitle: Baked sweet potatoes topped with seasoned beef, Greek yogurt, and cheese, topping-bar style
description: Whole sweet potatoes are baked until tender, split, and loaded with seasoned chili-style beef, Greek yogurt, shredded cheese, and a topping bar of scallions, black beans, and salsa. Everyone builds their own.

steps.title: Bake the sweet potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rub potatoes with olive oil, pierce a few times with a fork, and bake directly on a rack or sheet pan 45–55 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Brown the beef filling
steps.instruction: While potatoes bake, brown ground beef in a skillet over medium-high 7–8 minutes until no pink remains. Drain excess fat, stir in taco seasoning with 1/4 cup water, and simmer 3 minutes.

steps.title: Warm the black beans into the filling
steps.instruction: Fold drained black beans into the seasoned beef and simmer 3–4 minutes until heated through. This keeps the filling scoopable instead of two separate components on the plate.

steps.title: Hold potatoes and filling hot
steps.instruction: Wrap finished potatoes loosely in foil to hold their heat, and keep the beef-bean filling covered at 140°F or above. Do not let potatoes sit uncovered — they dry out fast.

steps.title: Set the topping bar
steps.instruction: Put Greek yogurt, cheddar, green onions, salsa, diced tomato, and jalapeño in separate bowls at the end of the line, keeping the yogurt and cheese cold until service starts.

steps.title: Split and load the potatoes
steps.instruction: Slice each potato lengthwise and press the ends toward the middle to open it up. Spoon in the beef-bean filling first so the base of the bowl holds heat.

steps.title: Finish loading and serve
steps.instruction: Top with cheddar so it melts slightly into the hot filling, then add Greek yogurt, salsa, tomato, and green onions. Serve immediately so the yogurt stays cool against the hot potato.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover seasoned beef and black bean filling — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool seasoned beef and black bean filling and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Bake a few extra potatoes — they reheat well and let latecomers build their own.
Rookie tip: Use Greek yogurt in place of sour cream; it holds up better once it hits the hot filling.
Swap the beef filling for seasoned black beans only to make the whole tray vegetarian.
Score the potato flesh lightly with a fork before loading so toppings settle in instead of sliding off.
tonightSpread: Sides: Simple green salad, tortilla chips
Condiments: Extra salsa, hot sauce, lime wedges
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool seasoned beef and black bean filling in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Scoop leftover potato flesh and filling into a quick skillet hash the next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It turns a familiar loaded-potato format into a higher-protein, better-balanced dinner without losing the comfort-food feel, and the topping bar handles picky eaters without extra cooking.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: bake potatoes and cook the beef filling up to two days ahead. Storage: keep potatoes, beef, and cold toppings in separate containers up to 4 days. Reheating: reheat potatoes and beef separately to 165°F, then rebuild with cold toppings.
substitutions: Use lean ground turkey instead of beef.
Use shredded rotisserie chicken tossed in taco seasoning for a lighter filling.
Skip the cheese and add extra black beans for a lower-fat version.
